title: CruxBench: A Benchmark of Information Discovery

evidence.label: 明确提出新的评测资料或框架
evidence.excerpt: To evaluate this capability of information discovery, we introduce CruxBench, a benchmark that grades LLM-generated questions by their Value of Information (VOI): how much a model-proposed crux updates beliefs about a target forecasting question.

evidence.label: 描述任务、问题或评测环境
evidence.excerpt: But a central step in many complex real-world tasks is identifying which questions are worth asking in the first place: decomposing a difficult problem into subquestions -- which we call cruxes -- whose answers provide key steps on the path toward solving the target problem.

evidence.label: 描述评分指标或评测协议
evidence.excerpt: Benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) typically evaluate the accuracy of answers against fixed reference labels.

evidence.label: 报告基线或多个模型的评测
evidence.excerpt: We evaluate a diverse set of eight models on 293 target forecasting questions and find that VOI correlates highly with independent measures of model capability (r=0.90) and captures cruxes' usefulness for answering target questions.

evidence.label: 给出任务规模或覆盖范围
evidence.excerpt: We evaluate a diverse set of eight models on 293 target forecasting questions and find that VOI correlates highly with independent measures of model capability (r=0.90) and captures cruxes' usefulness for answering target questions.

evidence.label: 讨论泛化、污染、稳健性或人工核验
evidence.excerpt: CruxBench enjoys a rare combination of three key properties: it is (1) contamination-resistant by construction, since ground truth is generated by future world events; (2) open-ended, admitting unbounded and complex text-based submissions rather than one correct numeric answer; and (3) grounded, with informativeness measured against quantified changes in real-world beliefs.
